articleBody:
Getting ready to expand your kitchen footprint requires locking down key specifications before construction begins. Use this pre-construction checklist to keep your project organized.

- [ ] Property boundary survey map — confirms zoning setback limits so the foundation does not cross legal easements or property lines.
- [ ] Stamped architectural and structural plan set — provides precise framing, roof tie-in, and foundation details required by your local building department.
- [ ] Written building permit application package — guarantees that municipal plan reviewers inspect and approve structural, mechanical, plumbing, and electrical drawings before breaking ground.
- [ ] Final appliance specification sheets — gives the framing and rough-in trades exact electrical voltage, gas line sizes, and ventilation rough openings.
- [ ] Cabinet layout order confirmation — prevents costly layout adjustments caused by ordering cabinets before framing dimensions and finish walls are locked.
- [ ] Subcontractor trade allocation sheet — clarifies who handles licensed plumbing, electrical hookups, framing, drywall, and finish carpentry.
- [ ] Site grading and drainage plan — ensures exterior stormwater drains away from the new kitchen foundation rather than pooling against walls.
- [ ] Certificate of contractor insurance — verifies active general liability coverage before heavy equipment or demolition crews arrive on your property.

How to use this checklist:
Review these items directly with your general contractor during the planning phase. Addressing these specifics early protects your home from unnecessary redesign fees, inspection delays, or costly rough-in relocations. When you are ready to expand your kitchen, contact HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866 to discuss your scope.
